harvested_sources.title: Suppressing quantum errors by scaling a quantum error-correcting code
harvested_sources.excerpt: We demonstrate that scaling a rotated surface code from distance 3 to distance 7 suppresses logical error rates by a factor of 3.8 per code distance step, conclusively operating below the fault-tolerant threshold.

harvested_sources.title: Fault-tolerant quantum computation with dynamic neutral atom arrays
harvested_sources.excerpt: Using 256 neutral rubidium atoms in reconfigurable optical tweezer arrays, we synthesize 48 dual-rail encoded logical qubits and execute non-abelian anyon braiding operations with transversal gates.

harvested_sources.title: Demonstration of high-fidelity logical entanglement in a 32-qubit QCCD processor
harvested_sources.excerpt: Quantinuum H2 trapped-ion platform achieves 99.914% physical two-qubit gate fidelity and demonstrates 32 logical qubits entangled with arbitrary single-qubit rotation synthesis.

harvested_sources.title: Fault-tolerant qLDPC architecture on heavy-hex lattices
harvested_sources.excerpt: IBM demonstrated 16 logical qubits encoded using bivariate bicycle qLDPC codes, achieving a 10x physical qubit footprint reduction compared to standard surface codes.

verified_claims.claim_statement: Superconducting surface codes operate below the fault-tolerant threshold with logical lifetime exceeding physical coherence.
Neutral atom optical tweezer systems have demonstrated 48 logical qubits with transversal gate operations.
Trapped ion hardware leads the industry in raw two-qubit physical gate fidelity at 99.914%.
qLDPC codes reduce physical-to-logical qubit ratio from 1000:1 to under 100:1.
contra_evidence: Requires non-planar 3D interconnects on planar superconducting chips.

quantitative_datapoints.metric: Logical Error Suppression per Distance Step

key_takeaways: Fault-tolerance break-even milestone is firmly established experimentally.
Neutral atoms lead in logical qubit count (48) due to dynamic shuttling.
Trapped ions lead in 2Q gate fidelity (99.91%).
qLDPC codes represent the next scaling frontier to compress hardware footprints.
